newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-CARTER TAKES EARLY LEAD TWO MONTHS AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CARTER TAKES EARLY LEAD TWO MONTHS AFTER BRAIN OPERATION.

text.p: Nearly two months after a serious brain operation, Briton David Carter took a share of the early lead at the Cannes Open on Thursday with a three-under-par 68.
Carter endured an operation to remove fluid from the brain after collapsing in his room two days before the start of the Dubai Desert Classic.
"Everything feels fine and I'm back in business," said Carter, who is still troubled by short term memory loss.
"I had to ask the caddie the names of my playing partners in the pro-am soon after they told me them because I tend to forget things from five minutes ago.
"But I got the thinking side of my game right, the thing that I was most worried I'd forgotten."
Carter picked up birdies at the 10th, 13th and 17th holes to share the lead with compatriot Paul Broadhurst.
"I'm extremely happy because I didn't know what to expect coming back out on tour again," he said.

"I was a little bit nervous at the first, but it helped play with a couple of guys I knew really well and that relaxed me. It was a difficult day in the wind, difficult to get the clubs right, but I hit a lot of greens and didn't make too many mistakes."
Broadhurst paid tribute to his coach Bill Ferguson after carding four birdies and a bogey.
"I took on Bill as my coach 18 months ago and he spotted straight away I was swaying off the ball," Broadhurst said.
"Putting that right helped me play my best golf of my career last year and hopefully it's continuing to this year."

Former Ryder Cup stalwart Howard Clark missed his chance to share the early lead after a double bogey at the last while veteran Gordon J. Brand, who won back his tour card last year, came to grief on the last three holes.
Brand, who led early on, finished with two double bogeys and a trip bogey, hitting into the water on the final hole for a 76.
